dedupe_keys.name: electrolyser capex and efficiency data for potential and risks of hydrogen based e fuels in climate change mitigation

description: Jordan Everall and Falko Ueckerdt at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research compile electrolyser capital costs, efficiencies and supplementary technology assumptions from academic and industry literature. Their March 2021 Zenodo release provides an Excel spreadsheet, an R Markdown dashboard script and a text README, all free under CC BY 4.0. Entries distinguish electrolysis method, publication year, literature type and the oldest reference year, with present and future assumptions for small and large installations. Coverage follows the reviewed literature and is not a current worldwide procurement-price survey. These tables can parameterise hydrogen-production and e-fuel investment simulations, provided currency, size and reference-year conventions are checked. Repeated or projected literature estimates should not be treated as independent observed plant costs. The related Nature Climate Change paper supplies the study context. No catalogue parent explicitly includes this compilation, and files were not downloaded.
